newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Belgacom 1996 group net profit up 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Belgacom 1996 group net profit up 21 pct.

text.p: NOTE - Belgacom SA is 49 percent owned by a consortium comprising Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors. The remaining shares are held by the Belgian state. The company already announced provisional 1996 results in January.
ratios at Dec, 31, 1996: shareholders' equity and third party interests/balance sheet total 31.8 pct vs 29.5 pct
financial debt/shareholders equity and third party interests

Belgacom said in a statement that following the acquisition of stakes in other companies and the creation of new subsidiaries during the financial year 1996, the number of consolidated companies had increased from three to eight.
Belgacom's main subsidiaries were still Belgacom Mobile SA - which is 25 percent owned by U.S. AirTouch Communications Inc - and Belgacom Directory Services (BDS) SA.

The increase in Belgacom's turnover reflected continued "major growth" in mobile telephony, the increase in national telephone service through ISDN (Integrated Services Digital Network), subscription fees, mobile telephone traffic and an increase in international telephone business.
Belgacom noted that financial income no longer included income from investments involving the pension reserves which were now being managed by its pension fund, created in 1995.

Financial expenses were reduced to 5.6 billion francs in 1996 from 6.5 billion in 1995 because of lower interest rates, a change in the structure of financial debts and the use of new methods of financing.
At the end of 1996 the company had 4.67 million fixed line connections, up slightly from 4.63 million at the end of 1995. This represented a penetration rate of 46 percent.
Belgacom Mobile currently had a total of 440,000 customers, a rise from 410,172 customers at the end of 1996 and from 235,238 at the end of 1995, Belgacom said.
